newsitem.title: FRANCE: Carrefour results defy weak spending trend.
newsitem.headline: Carrefour results defy weak spending trend.

text.p: Hypermarkets group Carrefour defied a sluggish spending climate in France to report a jump in profit on Thursday for the first half of the year.
It said profit excluding tax and exceptional items rose 20 percent to 1.21 billion francs ($238.2 million) in the first six months of 1996 and predicted a similar increase for the full year.
Net profit bounded to 2.15 billion francs from 927 million in the first half of 1995, due to a special 936 million franc gain from the sale of its stake in U.S. retailer PriceCostco.
Carrefour's stock rallied 1.3 percent to 2,732 francs at midday, outracing the Paris bourse's blue chip CAC-40 index which was up 0.6 percent.
"It's up on the results and the previous sales figures," reported this week by the company showing an 8.7 percent sales rise for August, a trader said.
First-half turnover rose seven percent to 72.48 billion francs, and the company said in its earnings statement that it expected full year sales to exceed 155 billion francs.
Carrefour's business has thrived despite weak consumer spending not only in France but also in other key markets such as Spain, Argentina and Brazil.
The group, whose strategy has been to expand abroad to reduce its dependence on the French market, last year announced it owned more hypermarkets abroad than in France.
Chairman Daniel Bernard told a news conference on Thursday that the group had 254 hypermarkets at the end of June, including 117 in France.
He said Carrefour planned to expand at the rate of around 30 stores per year. "We have the cash," he said.
Store openings are scheduled for 1997 in Poland, Indonesia and Singapore.

Carrefour, which is free of debt, plans to invest eight billion francs this year -- two-thirds of it abroad -- up from 7.56 billion last year, he said. It invested 4.3 billion francs in the first half and generated 3.3 billion francs of cashflow. ($ = 5.078 French Francs)
